text:
Sam: FYI — since ~03:15 UTC the eu-west GPU pool queue depth has been climbing and tail latency is spiking. Grafana 'pool/queue headroom' panel shows queue_depth per pool rising from ~120 -> ~750 over 40m. Can anyone confirm whether this is autoscaler hysteresis / probe flapping or a real provisioning shortfall?

Sam: PromQL I'm eyeballing on the panel: `sum by(pool)(queue_depth{region="eu-west"})` and headroom query looks like `avg_over_time(headroom[5m])`. The anomaly correlates with increased `batch_size` variance in the same window.

Aisha: I'm on it. Pulling autoscaler logs now — looks like scale-up events didn't land for a few rounds. Seeing repeated failed node bindings around 03:18: `FailedScheduling: 0/10 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient gpu, 3 network plugin timed out`.

Jordan: hmm that's suspicious. Are we seeing any recent churn in the node pool (spot preemptions) or kube-proxy restarts? I saw a few kube-proxy restarts in eu-west earlier today in the infra feed.

Maya: I checked the KV-cache layer for model workers — we had a config tweak yesterday to relax prefix cache TTLs which can increase batch reuse and thus effective batch sizes. Could be that larger batches are increasing queue headroom consumption and pushing autoscaler to react slower.

autoscaler-bot: [03:20:12] scale-up request for eu-west-gpu-pool accepted -> target replicas=24 (current 12).

Aisha: But the accepted scale-up never fully provisioned — cloud provider API returned intermittent 500s during node creation window. I've opened a provider ticket and flagged it in #vendors. Attaching relevant excerpt: ```
2024-05-07T03:18:21Z ERROR createNode: provider API 500 InternalServerError -> retry
2024-05-07T03:19:05Z WARN  bindPod: network plugin timeout
```

Sam: Good catch. Two forks of mitigation: 1) tweak Grafana alert debounce and threshold to avoid noisy paging while provider recovers; 2) add short-term manual headroom (increase reserved capacity) to avoid client-facing latency. Thoughts?

Jordan: For (1) propose change: increase alert evaluation window from 5m -> 10m and add `for: 5m` to the alert rule so we don't page on transient API errors. Also add a secondary alert that watches `kube_node_status_condition{condition="Ready"}` drop by >5% in 10m so we can catch mass failures.

Maya: For (2) I can spin up 4 warm nodes in eu-west (dedicated pool) as a quick buffer — will cost extra but buys time. I'll also revert the TTL tweak if we confirm it's worsening batching.

Aisha: Confirmed provider still returning errors; support case #CLOUD-4122 open. Meanwhile I'm patching the autoscaler to retry node create with backoff and to emit an event metric `autoscaler.create.failures` so we can alert on provider create error rate.

Sam: Action items: Maya to provision 4 warm nodes (in flight), Jordan to update alert debounce/window (PR ok to merge after review), Aisha to ship autoscaler metric and keep tracking provider ticket. I'll update the incident notes and ping SRE if SLA risk looks likely. :thumbsup:

Maya: Provision started — estimate nodes ready ~14m.

Jordan: PR #3842 created to change alert rule and add the k8s-ready secondary alert. cc @oncall for review.

Sam: Thanks everyone. Let's reconvene in ~20m or when nodes come up. If anyone sees queue_depth still >600 after warm nodes land, ping me immediately.
